meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's essay. You entered a zero before anyone called me. Why?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
You didn't answer my question. Show me, and then answer it.
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
Six hundred and twelve at 11:52, seven hundred and ninety-four at 11:58. What date? And you still entered a zero before anyone called me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and nothing placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on why it went in before anyone called her. The fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because the meeting ended after three exchanges, well before her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing yet, though your version history with exact word counts and times was the right kind of evidence; it just had no date, so she couldn't check it.
What cost ground: You passed over her opening question about entering the zero before calling home, and each time you skipped it she got sharper and kept coming back to it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your edits at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM came close to that kind of late night, even without a date. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asks why the zero went in before anyone called her, admit in one sentence that it was wrong, then give her the version history with its date so she can check it herself.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
